 Print Schools across Meghalaya will remain closed on Friday, November 13, 2026, as the state government has declared a holiday to mark the traditional Wangala Festival, one of the most important cultural celebrations of the indigenous Garo community. The holiday will apply to all government, government-aided, and private educational institutions across the state. The decision will allow students, teachers, and other school staff to participate in the annual post-harvest celebrations and observe the festival with their families. With the holiday falling on a Friday, students and teaching staff will get an extended weekend. Regular classroom activities will resume according to the normal academic timetable after the holiday. Wangala Festival: Why is November 13 a school holiday in Meghalaya?
 Wangala, popularly known as the 100 Drums Festival, is the most prominent post-harvest celebration of the Garo community. The festival marks the completion of the agricultural harvest cycle and is observed to express gratitude to Misi Saljong, revered as the Great Giver and Sun God, for blessing the community with a successful harvest. The celebration holds considerable cultural and social importance among the Garos, bringing communities together through traditional music, dance, and rituals. It also reflects the close relationship between the indigenous community, its agricultural practices, and its cultural traditions. The festival is particularly known for its distinctive musical performances, in which groups of performers play traditional cylindrical horn drums known as Dama. The rhythmic beats are accompanied by traditional horn-blowing and synchronised folk dances. Participants dress in traditional Garo attire, often complemented by colourful feathered headgear. The collective performances form the central attraction of the celebrations and showcase the community's distinctive cultural identity. What does the school holiday mean for students and parents?
 The statewide holiday means that no regular classes will be conducted in government, government-aided, or private schools on November 13. Students and parents should plan their academic schedules accordingly, particularly if they have school-level assessments, practical activities, or project submissions scheduled around the date. Parents are advised to check with their respective school administrations regarding any internal examinations, assignment deadlines, or other academic activities that may require rescheduling. Since the holiday falls on a Friday, students will also have Saturday and Sunday following the festival holiday, resulting in a three-day break from regular classroom activities.
